Contributing Scientist/Principal Investigator Role and Responsibilities
Each Contributing Scientist (CS)/Principal Investigator (PI) is required to report any deviations or other circumstances that could affect the quality or integrity of the study to the Study Director in a timely manner for authorization/acknowledgement. 
Each CS/PI will provide a report addressing their assigned phase of the 2_6_cs_pi_list which will be included in the Final Report.
Dose formulation analysis data will be provided to the Study Director for interpretation and data will be included in respective sections of the Main Report.
Bioanalytical data will be provided to the CS/PI responsible for toxicokinetic analysis for interpretation and inclusion in their phase report.
The CS phase report will include a listing of computerized systems used in the conduct and/or interpretation of the assigned study phase (alternatively, listing of computerized systems may be provided to the Study Director for inclusion in the Final Report).
The PI phase report will include a Statement of Compliance; a Quality Assurance (QA) statement (if audited by a Quality Assurance Unit [QAU] other than that of the Testing Facility and if the applicable phase is GLP); the archive site for all records, samples, specimens, and reports generated from the phase (alternatively, details regarding retention of the material may be provided to the Study Director for inclusion in the Final Report), and a listing of critical computerized systems (with version numbers) used in the conduct and/or interpretation of the assigned study phase (alternatively, listing of computerized systems may be provided to the Study Director for inclusion in the Final Report).

Housing
Animals will be <<socially or individually>> housed (same sex and dosing group together) in a polycarbonate cage with bedding <<or>> polycarbonate caging with perforated flooring and bedding <<or>> sterile, bedded cages with ventilated rodent housing. The primary enclosure complies with the recommendations set forth in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (National Research Council 2011).
Housing conditions will be maintained except when animals are separated for study-specific procedures or as required for monitoring and/or health purposes, as deemed appropriate by Study Director and/or Clinical Veterinarian. Animals may be introduced to a new social partner during the study for veterinary, behavioral, or study design purposes. In case of incompatibility, animals may be housed individually.
Environmental Conditions
Animals will be housed in a temperature-controlled and humidity-monitored environment.
An automatic lighting system will be set to provide a 12-hour light/dark cycle, except during designated procedures.
Diet and Feeding
Certified Teklad™ 2014C rodent diet (14% protein) will be offered ad libitum. Animals may be fasted as required for study-specific procedures.
The diet is routinely analyzed by the manufacturer for contaminants to be within Testing Facility specifications. No contaminants are expected to be present at levels that would interfere with the outcome of the study.
Food analysis records will be maintained in the Testing Facility records.
Drinking Water
Drinking water will be provided ad libitum via on-site filtered deep well water source. 
The water is routinely analyzed for contaminants. No contaminants are expected to be present at levels that would interfere with the outcome of the study.
Water analysis records will be maintained in the Testing Facility records.
Enrichment
Treats and enrichment devices will be provided throughout the course of the study.
Veterinary Care
Veterinary care will be available throughout the course of the study and animals will be examined by veterinary staff as warranted by clinical signs or other changes. All veterinary examinations will be documented in the study records.
In the event that animals require veterinary intervention, the responsible veterinarian will make initial recommendations about treatment (including sample collection/analysis for diagnostic purposes) of the animal and/or alteration of study procedures, which must be approved by the Study Director. All interventions and recommended therapeutic treatments (including sample collection/analysis for diagnostic purposes), if any, will be properly documented in the study records.
If the condition of the animal(s) warrants significant therapeutic interventions (up to, and including, euthanasia), the Sponsor representative will be contacted, when possible, to discuss appropriate action. Under emergency situations, the Study Director and/or the responsible veterinarian will attempt to consult with the Sponsor representative prior to addressing the medical emergency; however, the Study Director and/or veterinarian have the authority to act immediately to alleviate suffering.
In the event of unexpected reactions or unforeseen deaths, the Sponsor representative will be fully and promptly informed of such events.

Masking/Blinding
During this study, in-life functional observational battery (FOB) assessments <<and detailed clinical observations>> will be conducted by Testing Facility personnel who are masked (blinded) to the animals’ group assignments.
Study personnel not involved with in-life FOB assessments <<and detailed clinical observations>> will be unmasked (not blinded) to the animals’ group assignments and will conduct the various other general study procedures (eg, housing maintenance, animal care, or animal restraint for procedures). Once an individual is unmasked, the individual will not participate in any future FOB assessments <<and detailed clinical observations>> for this study.
All other study activities will be conducted by either masked (blinded) or unmasked (not blinded) personnel.

Descriptive and Inferential Statistical Analyses
Means, standard deviations, and percent change from concurrent controls will be reported (excluding clinical pathology dataset where only mean and standard deviation will be reported), when appropriate and calculated using the full precision of the raw data.
All inferential statistical tests will be conducted at the 5% significance level.
The following table defines the set(s) of comparisons to be used in the statistical analyses described below for all study animals.
Descriptive and inferential analyses will be conducted on the variables listed below, but will exclude semi-quantitative data, and inferential analysis will also exclude any group with less than 3 values.
Homogeneity of variance will be tested using Bartlett’s test. If Bartlett’s test is statistically significant, a data transformation will be attempted by taking the log of the value and Bartlett’s testing will be repeated on the transformed data. If Bartlett’s test is not statistically significant on the raw data or transformed data, a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) will be applied. If the one-way ANOVA is significant, Dunnett’s test will be used to compare the mean values or transformed values from each dose of the test article with those of the 13_1_group_name. If Bartlett’s test yields a significant result, indicating heterogeneity of variance for both the raw data and transformed data, the data will be analyzed by Kruskal-Wallis’s H-test. If the Kruskal-Wallis’s H-test results are significant, Dunn’s modification to Steel’s test will be conducted.
Statistical Analysis for Functional Observational Battery Assessments
The following table defines the set(s) of comparisons to be used in the statistical analyses described below for all animals that participated in FOB assessments.
All FOB test parameters will be evaluated and categorized as continuous, count, graded, dichotomous, or descriptive. Based on the categorization, FOB test parameters will be evaluated based on the methodology described below.
The following analyses will be conducted separately for each testing phase (Acclimation, Dosing, and Recovery). The first evaluation will include all available dose groups (Groups 1, 2, 3, and 4 for the acclimation and dosing period and Groups 1 and 4 for the recovery period). If there is a significant overall difference among the groups, the pairwise comparisons of groups described in the above table will be conducted. All tests will be conducted at the 0.05 level and there will be no adjustment for multiple comparisons.
Continuous Data:
Each analysis endpoint will be analyzed with an Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) including the fixed effect for treatment group (TRT). If the TRT effect is significant, the defined pairwise comparisons of groups will be conducted.
Count Data:
Count data will be transformed using square-root transformation and analyzed by the methodology described for continuous data.
Graded Response:
Each analysis endpoint will be analyzed with the extended Mantel-Haenszel (MH) test. Integer scores will be used, and the alternative hypothesis will be that of a mean score shift (row mean scores differ). The alternative hypothesis will consider the ordinal scale of the response variable. If the overall (all groups) test is significant, the defined pairwise comparisons of groups will be conducted.
Dichotomous Response:
Each analysis endpoint will be analyzed using Fisher's exact test. If the overall (all groups) test is significant, the defined pairwise comparisons of groups will be conducted.
Descriptive Response:
Each descriptive categorical data endpoint will be summarized by tables showing the numbers of animals included in each category for each dose group. No inferential statistics will be conducted.

Appendix  - Study Design Guidance
<<Non-GLP>>
The study design and scope were based on the study objective and the overall product development strategy for the test article.
<<GLP>>
The study design and scope were based on both the study objective(s) as well as the following guidelines:
International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) M3(R2), “Non-clinical safety studies for the conduct of human clinical trials and marketing authorization for pharmaceuticals”.
ICH S3a, “Note for Guidance on Toxicokinetics: The Assessment of Systemic Exposure in Toxicity Studies”.
ICH S4, “Duration of Chronic Toxicity Testing in Animals (Rodent and Non Rodent Toxicity Testing)”.
ICH S6(R1), “Preclinical Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology-Derived Pharmaceuticals”.
ICH S9, “Nonclinical Evaluation for Anticancer Pharmaceuticals”.
ICH S7A, “Guideline on Safety Pharmacology Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals”.
ICH S8, “Immunotoxicity Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals”.
Justification for Species Selection and Number of Animals
This species was selected because it is commonly used for nonclinical research and is an accepted rodent species for nonclinical toxicity evaluations by regulatory agencies.
Rodents show reproducible growth rates under laboratory conditions, are reasonably free from extraneous diseases, and have a low level of spontaneous abnormalities.
The total number of animals is the minimum needed to properly characterize responses related to test article administration and, thus, to meet experimental objectives.
Justification for the Selection of Route, Frequency, and Dose Level
This administration route of exposure is consistent with the proposed route of administration in humans.
Dose levels were selected based on previous studies with animals, as a range from near expected therapeutic levels in the clinic to high multiples of the anticipated human dosage.

Procedure Details
Anesthesia | Animals will be induced and maintained with isoflurane. Animals will be maintained on a warming pad throughout the surgical procedure and during the recovery period. The animals will be monitored until fully recovered and returned to their home cage once ambulatory. Anesthesia procedures will be documented and retained in the study data.
Analgesia | 8_4_Analgesia_specie
Animals will be given analgesic treatments as appropriate for invasive procedures. If any pain or distress is observed following a study procedure, the animal(s) will be assessed by a Testing Facility veterinarian and treated appropriately in consultation with the Study Director. Treatments will be documented and retained in the study data.
Antibiotics | Enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg, SC).
Antibiotics will be administered at the time of procedure for prophylaxis treatment. Treatments will be documented in the study data.
Procedure Details
Mortality/moribundity check | At least twice daily (AM and PM; with at least 4 hours between observations).
To assess general animal health and wellness (except on the first and last day of the study where it will be conducted at least once).
Cage Side Observations | Once daily, beginning Day/Week X of acclimation, and at X hours (± 1 hour) after dosing <<close to Tmax>>/post end of infusion on dosing days9_1_CageSideObservations_days
Additional cage side observations may be conducted as necessary to properly monitor the animal’s health condition.
Detailed Clinical Observations | Once during acclimation (prior to randomization), on Day -1, then once weekly thereafter throughout the study, including prior to necropsy.
Additional detailed clinical observations may be conducted as necessary to properly monitor the animal’s health condition.
Injection Site Observations | Once on Day 1 (predose), and once daily/weekly at X hours (±1 hour) postdose.
Procedure Details
Modified Draize Dermal Scoring | Daily, beginning on Day 1 (prior to dose).
Dose sites will be observed for skin irritation using the Modified Draize scoring system detailed below.
Category | Score | Description
Erythema | 0 | None
Erythema | 1 | Slight
Erythema | 2 | Well-defined
Erythema | 3 | Moderate or severe
Erythema | 4 | Severe or slight eschar formation (injuries in depth)
Edema | 0 | None
Edema | 1 | Very slight
Edema | 2 | Slight (well-defined edges)
Edema | 3 | Moderate (raised > 1 mm)
Edema | 4 | Severe (raised > 1 mm and extending beyond the area of exposure)
Procedure Details
Body Weight | At least once during acclimation (prior to randomization) <<and on Day -1>>, then once weekly thereafter throughout the study, including the day prior to necropsy. For animals euthanized at an unscheduled interval, a body weight will be collected prior to necropsy, when possible.
Additional body weights may be taken, if necessary.
Terminal Body Weight | Terminal body weights will be collected on the day of scheduled necropsy from 9_2_species_fasted_status for the purpose of calculating organ-to-body weight ratios. No terminal body weight will be collected from animals found dead.
Procedure Details
Food Consumption | At least weekly, beginning on Day 1.
Food consumption will be derived from the supplied and remaining amounts of feed. The average gram(g)/animal/day will be calculated from the weekly food consumption.
Procedure Details
Ophthalmology | Once during the acclimation period and during the last week of the dosing period and recovery periods9_4_ophthalmology_period
Topical mydriatic (1% Tropicamide) will be administered. Both eyes will be examined using an indirect ophthalmoscope by a board-certified Ophthalmologist.
Procedure Details
Functional Observational Battery Assessments | Once prior to dose administration, then at 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_PostDoseAssessmentHours hours(± 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_PostDoseAssessmentMinutesWindow) and 24 hours following dose administration on 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_AssessmentDayOrWeekReference, and during the 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_AssessmentDayOrWeekNumber week of the recovery period.
Functional Observational Battery (FOB) assessments, which include 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_AssessmentComponents, will be conducted by trained 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_BlindingDetails’ group assignments on 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_GroupAssignmentClarification. FOB assessments will be conducted for each animal at each time point beginning with the 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_ObservationSequence. The start of the FOB assessment per animal at each time point will be defined as the 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_StartTimeDefinition. All 9_6_FunctionalObservationalBatteryAssessments_ScoringMethod at each time point and scores will be assigned.
Assessments | Animals will be individually housed 9_6_Assessments_IndividualHousingPreAssessmentDuration prior to FOB assessments to allow for acclimation to individual housing and will be individually housed during the assessments.
Animals will be observed in the home cage for 9_6_Assessments_HomeCageParameters. Animals will then be removed from the home cage to assess 9_6_Assessments_HandlingParameters. Animals will then be placed in an open  field-testing box and observed for a 9_6_Assessments_OpenFieldTestDuration to assess 9_6_Assessments_OpenFieldParameters.
For sensorimotor observations, animals will remain in the open field-testing box or will be taken to a dedicated testing station and will be assessed for 9_6_Assessments_SensorimotorParameters. Physiological assessments, including 9_6_Assessments_PhysiologicalParameters will also be assessed.
